questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Accessibility to campus during COVID has been very good in Norway; courses in english; different approaches to study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good. Would recommend archaeological migration studies, celtic mythological texts and runology to any archaeology student.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had buddy groups in an introduction week, our "buddies" were very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It should be mentioned to anyone interested in studying abroad with erasmus, that the work predating the exchange itself (forms, deadlines and such) is very time-consuming and there is little to no help from either the Erasmus officers or the exchange secretaries at the university of Copenhagen in working though this ridiculous amount of bureaucracy. Deadlines are often announced at very short notice and in the middle of the exam period. All I´m saying is... be prepared! For most people, it will be incredibly stressful to arrange their exchange, if youre also studying and working at the same time.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very, very hard. I was on the point of cancelling my visit because of limited housing, and there is no help from SiO, the relevant institution. I began searching for housing in march, and didnt find anything till august, the week before I left (I was lucky that my parents have norwegian friends). If you already know/consider going to Oslo, start looking right away!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live a little outside town; Oslo is great because it is no close to nature, so take advantage fo that, if you cant find a place on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of help available from both professors and secretaries.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very - well, there was som bureaucracy in registering for courses taught in norwegian, those apparently werent offered to foreign students, then it was offered, but by that time I had already had to switch courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most things can be fixed - just be paitient and spam the secretaries.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very high. A lot of foreign professors with widely different focuses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much better - very comparative, almost anthropological approach.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Archaeological Migration Studies.
Celtic Mythological Texts.
Runology; general introduction.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above.

questions.answer: Transport, vegetables and books were very expensive. Meat was cheaper.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many - but I didnt attend any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cant really say much.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Bergen with the train! Or travel to Northern Norway!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy; but Denmark and Norway are relatively similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend social clubs, live on campus, go out, be active in the buddy week.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Getting to know people is harder in Scandinavia, it just takes more time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That norwegians loooove Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare for UCPH bureaucracy!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Minimize living costs! Have a stable financial base, because you will spend more than you earn during the exchange.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The teaching!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to know people

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
